title: QuadraticFloor: quadratic floor sums and the trace of a quartic Bernoulli number
abstract: For an odd prime p and integers A, B, C, the alternating floor sum S_{A,B,C}(p) is the sum over 0 <= n < p of (-1)^floor((A n^2 + B n + C)/p). The development proves the root-count reduction of S_{A,B,C}(p) to a sum of Legendre symbols over an arithmetic progression when A + B is even, and, for a positive odd A, an odd prime p not dividing A and an admissible pair (B odd, prime to A, 1 <= B^2 - 4AC < 4A), the square-class decomposition: S_{A,B,C}(p) equals (-1)^C minus the average over the Dirichlet characters psi modulo A of conj(psi(B))^2 times the first Bernoulli number, at modulus 8Ap, of the odd character eta_p chi_{-4}^{delta} psi, where eta_p is the Kronecker character of discriminant -8p. Consequently the sum depends only on the square class of B modulo A. At A = 1 and A = 3 this gives the floor sums in terms of Bernoulli numbers of quadratic characters (which are class numbers by Dirichlet's formula, not formalized). At A = 5 the difference S_{5,3,0}(p) - S_{5,1,0}(p) is the real part of the first Bernoulli number of the quartic character Theta_p = eta_p chi_{-4} xi of conductor 40p, with xi(2) = i; this real part is an even integer whose residue modulo 4 is given by an explicit indicator z_1 - z_3. Finally the sums with A = 1 and fixed shifts a, b are classified: for odd a in terms of S_{1,1,0}(p) and an oriented sum of Legendre symbols, for even a by an explicit finite formula that is bounded and eventually constant in p.
